terms.fr: Pays où la langue est officielle
terms.ro: Țări în care limba este oficială

en.title: Countries with official status
en.summary: Where English has an official place in law and government.

paragraphs: English is official, or the main working language, in many countries. This lesson shows where, explains what official language means and teaches pairs of conjunctions that link choices.

The United Kingdom has no law that names an official language, but English is used by government everywhere. The United States has no official language at the federal level either, although English is used in nearly all government business. Canada has two official languages, English and French. Ireland has two as well, Irish and English. Australia, New Zealand, South Africa, India, Nigeria and Singapore also give English an important official role. Two students prepare a quiz.

lines.speaker: Nia
lines.text: Is English the official language of the United States?

lines.speaker: Ravi
lines.text: Not at the federal level. The constitution doesn't name one, though many states have declared English official.

lines.speaker: Ravi
lines.text: Canada has two official languages: English and French.

lines.speaker: Ravi
lines.text: Hindi and English are both used for official business, and there are twenty-two other recognised languages.

lines.speaker: Nia
lines.text: So a country can have several official languages.

lines.speaker: Ravi
lines.text: Yes, South Africa has eleven, and English is the main one in government and business.

paragraphs: **1. Both... and, either... or and neither... nor link choices.** Both... and joins two things that are true; either... or offers a choice; neither... nor denies both. See Introduction to Grammar: Prepositions and conjunctions.

blocks.html:
PairExample
both... andBoth English and French are official.
either... orYou can use either English or Hindi.
neither... norNeither language is dominant.
not only... but alsoIt is not only official but also widely spoken.

paragraphs: **2. Degree words describe how true a statement is.** Almost all, nearly all and not at all show different degrees. See Introduction to Grammar: Adverbs.

blocks.html:
WordExample
almost allAlmost all offices use English.
mostMost states have an official language.
not at allIt is not official at all.
hardly anyHardly any laws mention it.

items: Official language means the language of laws, courts and government.
Federal means belonging to the central government of a federation such as the United States.
A language can be official without being named in a law.
A working language is used in daily government business.

paragraphs: Many countries where English is official have other languages used at home, such as Welsh, Gaelic, Maori, Hindi, Yoruba or Spanish. English often serves as the language that unites people with different mother tongues.
